2. The prosecution case, to narrate in brief, is that on 10-5-2002 at 10-30 AM in the morning Md Saidur Rahman Newton (victim), one of the sons of the informant set out for 'Sugondha Community Centre' 'to attend the Wedding ceremony of, Engineer Shafiqur Rahrhan; another son of the informant being accompanied by Md Kazi Ismail and Md Mizan, the body-guard and the driver of the rented Micro-bus. On his way to the Community Centre the victim went to the first floor of 'Orchid Plaza' situated at Dhanmondi to get his hair dressed. At 11-00 AM Ismail informed one Md Hanif, the nephew of the informant over mobile phone that Piyal Sagar, Boltu Russell, Siptil, Dilip Babu, Faruque, Rangu and some other persons gintned down Saidur Rahman Newton in front of the maingate of 'Orchid Plaza'. Hearing the news, the informant along With her husband, son Tapan and nephew Hanif rushed to the place Of occurrence and came to know that her son Newton was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in injured condition. The informant went to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and found her son Saidur Rahman Newton, the victim dead. She also found Ismail, the body-guard of the deceased and the driver lying there sustaining bullet injury. On query, Ismail disclosed that at 11-40 AM when they came to the ground floor of 'Orchid Plaza' after dying hair of, the victim Saidur Rahman Newton from 'Shitol Saloon', the accused-persons' Sagar, Boltu Russell, Dilip Babu, Faruq, Rangu and some other persons shot him on the head and on the different parts of the person of Saidur Rahman Newton. When Ismail and the driver Mizan went forward to protect Newton they also received bullet injuries. The victim's political rivals who laced defeat in the City Corporation election have killed the victim at the instigation of Asa Khan, Minto, Rahat Khan and Mosharraf Hossain. 

 24. The PW 10 Jagannath Das Khokan stated in his deposition that on 25-05-2002 in accordance with the provisions of sections 164 and 364 of the Code of Criminal Procedure he recorded the confessional Statement (Exhibit-4) of the accused Md Rubel Hossain Howlader as per High Court From No. M84. He certified the confessional statement after recording the same. On 10-10-2002 in accordance with the provisions of sections 164 and 364 of the Code of Criminal Procedure he recorded the confessional statement (Exhibit-4) of the accused Md Aiyub as per the High Court form No. M84 (Exhibit-5) certified this confessional statement as such the same. This witness proved the confessional statements of the accused-persons Md Rubel Hossain Howlader and. Md Aiyub Ali, their signatures and his signatures therein as Exhibits, 4, 4/1-4/3, 4/4-4/10, 5, 5/1-5/3 and 5/4-5/9 respectively. In his cross this witness stated that after the statements were read over to the accused-persons they put their signatures therein. He himself wrote the certificates. The accused-persons made statements sitting in the chair. On 10-3-2003 the Investigating Officer went the accused Shawkat Hossain to him for recording his statement under section 164 of the Code of criminal Procedure. But in view of expression of ignorance about the occurrence by the accused Shawkat Hossain his statement was not recorded. He could not recollect as to whether the word 'Abbas' was written in different ink subsequently at the page No. 4 of the confessional statement of the accused Md Aiyub. The word 'Abbas' which was under-lined twice was written outside the margin of the statement. He did not put his signature at the margin. The accused Rubel did not mention the name of the accused Abbas in his statement. This witness denied the defence-suggestions that the confessional statements of the Accused-persons Md Rubel Hossain Howlader and Md Aiyub were not true and voluntary or that those statements were procured by torture and allurement. 

 On dissection there was haemotoma in Lt. partial and occipital areas. Skull perforated through Tr. frontal bone. The meninges are perforated. Brain found lacerated in both parital and frontal lobes. Subdura and sub arachmoid and intra-cerebral heamorrhage noted. Inter costal muscles of Rt. chest and the Rt. plura are perforated at different sides. Both small and large gut are ruptured. The spleen and It. Kidney found ruptured. Lt Hummers in its middle 3rd found fractured. 

 30. The PW 15 SI Sheikh Mahar Rahman stated in his disposition that on 10-5-2002 he was attached to Dhanmondi Police Station. As per the instruction of the officer-in-charge vide Dhaka Metropolitan Police station GDE No. 1502 dated 10-5-2002 he went to morgue, Dhaka Medical College Hospital at 15.00 hours taking constable No. 10241 Abdul Matin with him. As per identification of Md Anisur Rahman, the brother of the deceased Newton he held inquest on the dead body of Newton in presence of the witnesses and prepared Inquest report. During inquest he found as many as 22 marks of bleeding injuries starting from the forehead to the whole body of Newton. He found marks of blood injuries on the forehead, mouth, belly and thigh and at the different parts of the body. After preparation of Inquest Report he sent the dead body for post mortem examination through constable Matin. This witness proved the Inquest Report as Exhibit-9, and his signature therein as Exhibit-9(2), the chalan and his signature therein as Exhibit-8(3). In his cross this witness stated that at the time of holding inquest he did not find any bandage on the person of the deceased. He found entrance of bullet on the person of the deceased. He did not mention mark of exit in the report. He started writing the report by putting date. The attesting witnesses of the inquest report were the inhabitants of Mirpur. 

 35. Now, the question is whether in furtherance of their common intention the aforesaid accused-persons killed the deceased Newton. From the evidence on record, it is also found that on the date of occurrence after contacting with each other the aforesaid accused-persons in a body went to the place of occurrence with a micro bus and a private car. Some of them remained in vigilance at different place for facilitating the perpetration of the alleged occurrence and to defend others and some of them directly took part in the killing of the deceased Newton. Said facts definitely suggest the common intention of the aforesaid accused-persons to kill the deceased Newton even if some accused-persons did no open fire targeting the deceased. In this regard the learned DAG referred the case of Md Bazlul Huq vs The State reported in decision reported in 18 BLT (AD) at page 3 in which our apex Court held that "A" criminal intention within the meaning of section 34 of the Penal Code is simultaneous conscientious of the mind of the persons participating in the criminal action to bring such particular result and if one facilitates the execution of the common design such person commits an offence as much as his co-participants actually committing the planned crime. The essence of the section is that the persons must be coupled with actual participation, which may be of passive character such as standing by a door or near about the incident with the intention of assisting in furtherance of common intention of all the accused and with readiness to play his part when the time comes for him to act. The dominant feature of section 34 of the Penal Code is the element of participation in actions. This participation need not in all cases be by physical presence. Common intention implies acting in concert; This section requires that there must be a general intention shared by all these persons united with a common purpose to do any criminal offence, all of these who assist in the accomplishment of the object would be equally guilty. It follows, therefore, that common intention is an intention to commit a crime actually committed and every one of them should have participated in that crime". In this connection the case of State vs Abul Khair reported in 44 DLR at page 284 may also be referred. In the said case it is held that "In order to attract section 34 of the Penal Code it is not necessary that any overt act must be dome by any particular accused. The provision shall be applicable if it is established that the criminal act has been done by any one of these accused-persons in furtherance of the common intention of all. Mere distance from the scene of the crime cannot exclude culpability. Criminal sharing by active presence or by distance direction, making out certain measure of jointness in the commission of the act is the essence of section 34". In the context of the present case we are in respectful agreement with the aforesaid decisions. So, our answer to the question as to whether the aforesaid accused-persons killed the deceased Newton in furtherance of their common intention is in the positive. Be it mentioned here that the accused-persons Md Khorshed, Sahadat Hossain alias Sahadat, Kala Zahangir, Kazi Towfiq Alam alias Piyal, Sadekul Islam Chowdhury alias Sagar, Munir Hossain alias Kiran and Kazi Md Ismail remained absconding during trial of the case and are still absconding without preferring any appeal against the impugned judgment and order. This conduct of the said accused-persons is a relevant fact which should be taken into consideration as a circumstance in determining their guilty and also their involvement in the alleged occurrence. In this regard, the learned DAG referred the case of Monsur Ali vs the State reported in 55 DLR (AD) at page 131 in which case our apex Court held that "A fugitive has no right to seek any kind of redress as against his grievance, if any, against the judgment and order of a Court convicting him to imprisonment". We are in respectful agreement with the said decision. 

 38. On perusal of the statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure made by the accused Shawkat Hossain, it appears that said statement was not made in connection with the present case, rather, it was made in connection with the Pallabi PS Case No. 29(07)02. Further, the statement appears to be a Photostat copy not proved in accordance with the provisions of the Evidence Act law. The PW 9 Md Suajayet Ullah who recorded the aforesaid statement stated in his evidence that through the CMM the accused Shawkat Hossain was sent to him for recording statement under 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with the present case but in view of his saying that he did not know any thing about the occurrence, his statement was not recorded. So, that said statement of the accused Shawkat Hossain deserves no consideration in this case. From the evidence of the PWs, it appears that none of them disclosed the participation of the accused Md Abbas alias Killer Abbas in their evidence in the alleged occurrence. It has already been stated that the confessional statement of the accused Shawkat Hossain deserves no consideration in this case. Further, as per the evidence of the PW 10 Jagannath Das Khokan the name of Md Abbas was underlined twice in the statement of accused Aiyub and that the name of Abbas was written outside the margin and that there was signature of him in the margin. The PW 10 also said that the name of the accused Abbas did not appear in the confessional statement of the accused Md Aiyub and that he did not recollect as to whether the name of Abbas was written subsequently in different ink in the first paragraph of page No. 4 of the confessional statement of the accused Md Aiyub. In view of the facts as stated so far, these is doubt about the participation of the accused Abbas Ali alias killer Abbas in the alleged occurrence. As far as the accused-persons Zakir Hossain Khan and Sheikh Kamal Hossain alias Md Kamal Hossain are concerned no confessing accused-persons implicated them in the alleged occurrence. Although the PW 5 implicated the accused Zakir Hossain and Kamal in the alleged occurrence, the PW 4 did not implicate the accused Md Kamal Hossain in the alleged occurrence. None of the other PWs implicated the said accused-persons in the alleged occurrence. With regard to the accused Md Ibrahim Khalil alias Ibrahim no eye-witness implicated him in the alleged occurrence and that although the accused Md Aiyub implicated the accused Md Ibrahim in the alleged occurrence, no other confessing accused implicated him in the alleged occurrence. With regard to the accused Nazmul Hossain alias Benga Babu no eye-witness implicated him in the alleged occurrence. Further, although the accused Md Aiyub stated the name of the accused Md Nazmul Hossain alias Benga Babu in his confessional statement, the accused Md Rubel Hossain Howlader did not implicate him in the alleged occurrence. So, from the discussion made so far, we are of the opinion that the charge as brought against the accused persons Shawkat Hossain, Md Abbas Ali alias Killer Abbas, Zakir Hossain Khan, Sheikh Kamal Hossain alias Md Kamal Hossain, Md Ibrahim Khalil alias Ibrahim and Nazmul Hossain alias Benga Babu could not be substantiated beyond all reasonable doubt and, as such, they are entitled to the benefit of doubt and an order of acquittal in this case.
